name: Kadiatou Lund-Bangura
role: Field trauma surgeon and combat support — combat medic
location: The Spires — mid-level corporate residential towers
description:
Kadiatou Lund-Bangura is broad-shouldered and heavy, carrying their weight like armor rather than burden. At 52, his face is memorable in a profession that rewards forgettability, and he has learned to compensate. The chrome is visible — cybernetic arm — right, full replacement from shoulder — stronger than organic,  — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He grew up in the Narrows, where the walls are so close together you learn to fight in confined spaces or you learn to lose. He works as a combat medic out of The Spires, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

What Kadiatou Lund-Bangura lacks in subtlety, he compensates for in thoroughness. No loose ends, no unfinished business, no second chances.

core_fears: Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine
Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome
That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability
core_desires: Freedom from augmentation debt — the interest compounds like a tumor
Knowledge — to understand the systems that grind people down
To build something that outlasts the next contract cycle
coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation
Compartmentalization — work feelings and personal feelings exist in separate boxes
blind_spots: Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise
Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
psychology.secret: Kadiatou Lund-Bangura is slowly going chrome-sick — rejection symptoms are manageable now but getting worse. Has maybe two years before it becomes visible.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Warm and personable on the surface, with an undertone that suggests the warmth is a professional tool.
speech_patterns.cadence: Low and even — the vocal equivalent of still water.
verbal_tics: Hums tunelessly when planning — the team has learned to wait for the humming to stop
Uses 'we' instead of 'I' — either royal or dissociative, nobody asks
example_lines: "Hold still. This is going to hurt and I don't care."
"I can keep you alive through almost anything. What I can't do is make you grateful."
"Blood type? No, I don't need your blood type. I need you to stop moving."

story_hooks: A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Kadiatou Lund-Bangura's reputation — and a price for silence
A crew member from Kadiatou Lund-Bangura's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
Someone is impersonating Kadiatou Lund-Bangura on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original
narrative_function: Kadiatou Lund-Bangura functions as a connector — his work puts him in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving him naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
augmentations: Cybernetic arm — right, full replacement from shoulder — stronger than organic, obvious chrome. Thermal masking system — body heat signature can be suppressed or spoofed
daily_life: Irregular schedule dictated by contract timing. Between jobs: equipment maintenance, physical training, and the careful management of a reputation that exists entirely through word of mouth. Drinks at establishments where runners gather — not for pleasure, but for market intelligence.
affiliation: Semi-independent — recurring contracts with mid-tier fixers

strengths: photographic memory for faces and layouts
weaknesses: trust issues that limit crew effectiveness
old injury that flares under specific conditions

decision_rules: Will abandon a job if the intel was deliberately falsified — being set up violates the contract
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Guarded respect. They pay, the job gets done. Anything beyond that is liability.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Competitive but reliable. Will challenge decisions but never abandon the team.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Superficially friendly, internally cataloguing exits and weapons. The smile is real; the relaxation isn't.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation — checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Goes quiet. The silence is not calm — it's the sound of every contingency being evaluated simultaneously.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Despises corporate culture but has unconsciously adopted its efficiency metrics and self-optimization language
Claims to work only for money but regularly takes underpriced jobs that serve personal justice
habits: Maintains a dead drop with emergency supplies in three separate districts
Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
Checks exits within 10 seconds of entering any room
Keeps a physical paper notebook — no digital record of personal thoughts
breaking_points: Watching someone they trained or mentored die on a job they recommended
A child being put in danger as leverage against them
Running out of options — no contacts, no money, no safe house, no way out
